questions.name: Air Brakes
questions.text: Air brake systems use a specific component to generate the compressed air that operates the brakes. According to the CDL manual, what is the basic function of the air compressor in an air brake system?

answers.text: It pumps air into the air storage tanks (reservoirs)
It releases compressed air through the foot valve to apply the brakes
It converts hydraulic pressure into pneumatic pressure for the slack adjusters
It powers the spring brakes by mechanical force when the engine is off

explanations.a: The CDL manual states that the air compressor pumps air into the air storage tanks (reservoirs) and is connected to the engine through gears or a v-belt.
explanations.b: Air release at the foot valve happens through a separate brake pedal valve, not the compressor.
explanations.c: There is no hydraulic-to-pneumatic conversion in an air brake system; air is the only working fluid.
explanations.d: Spring brakes are held by mechanical springs, not powered by the compressor.

questions.name: Air Brakes
questions.text: The air compressor governor controls when the compressor pumps air into the storage tanks. According to the CDL manual, around what cut-out and cut-in pressures does the governor typically operate?

answers.text: Cut-out at about 60 psi, cut-in at about 30 psi
Cut-out at about 125 psi, cut-in at about 100 psi
Cut-out at about 150 psi, cut-in at about 125 psi
Cut-out at about 200 psi, cut-in at about 175 psi

explanations.a: 60 psi is the low-pressure-warning threshold, not the governor's cut-out point.
explanations.b: The CDL manual states the governor stops the compressor at the cut-out level around 125 psi and allows pumping again at the cut-in level around 100 psi.
explanations.c: 150 psi is the typical safety valve setting, not the governor cut-out.
explanations.d: 200 psi exceeds the typical air brake operating range; the safety valve would open well below that.

questions.name: Air Brakes
questions.text: A safety relief valve is installed in the first air tank to protect the system from overpressure. According to the CDL manual, at approximately what pressure is the safety valve usually set to open?

answers.text: About 60 psi
About 100 psi
About 150 psi
About 250 psi

explanations.a: 60 psi is the low-pressure-warning threshold, not the safety valve setting.
explanations.b: 100 psi is the typical governor cut-in pressure, not the safety valve setting.
explanations.c: The CDL manual states the safety valve is usually set to open at 150 psi to protect the tank and rest of the system from too much pressure.
explanations.d: 250 psi is well above the rated pressure of typical air brake components.

questions.name: Air Brakes
questions.text: Compressed air contains some water and oil that collect at the bottom of the air tanks. According to the CDL manual, what is the proper drainage practice for tanks equipped only with manual drain valves?

answers.text: Drain only when the safety valve releases air
Drain only when the air dryer indicator lamp illuminates
Drain monthly during routine preventive maintenance only
Drain the tanks completely at the end of each day of driving

explanations.a: Waiting for the safety valve to release air leaves accumulated water and oil in the tanks far too long.
explanations.b: There is no air-dryer indicator that controls manual draining in the manual's procedure.
explanations.c: Monthly draining is far less frequent than the manual's daily standard.
explanations.d: The CDL manual instructs drivers to drain manually-valved tanks completely at the end of each day of driving, because water can freeze in cold weather and cause brake failure.

questions.name: Air Brakes
questions.text: The CDL manual gives several alternate names for the brake pedal in an air brake system. Which set of names matches the manual's terminology?

answers.text: Brake pedal, foot valve, and treadle valve
Slack adjuster and brake chamber
Glad hand and tractor protection valve
S-cam and wedge driver

explanations.a: The CDL manual states the brake pedal is also called the foot valve or the treadle valve.
explanations.b: Slack adjuster and brake chamber are foundation-brake parts, not names for the pedal.
explanations.c: Glad hand and tractor protection valve are combination-vehicle plumbing components, not pedal names.
explanations.d: S-cam and wedge are brake-actuation mechanisms, not pedal names.

questions.name: Air Brakes
questions.text: The most common foundation brake on heavy commercial vehicles uses a specific cam shape that gives the device its name. According to the CDL manual, what is the s-cam, and how does it work in the brake?

answers.text: A spring-loaded cam that pushes a wedge between the brake pads
A cam shaped like the letter S that, when rotated by the slack adjuster, forces the brake shoes apart against the inside of the drum
A solenoid-actuated cam that triggers ABS during hard stops
A coiled cam used in air-over-hydraulic conversions for medium trucks

explanations.a: That is a wedge-brake description, not the s-cam.
explanations.b: The CDL manual describes the s-cam as a cam shaped like the letter S that, when rotated through the brake camshaft by the slack adjuster, forces the brake shoes apart against the inside of the brake drum.
explanations.c: ABS uses an electronic control unit and modulator valves, not a solenoid-actuated cam.
explanations.d: The s-cam is the standard mechanical actuator on heavy air brakes, not an air-over-hydraulic component.

questions.name: Air Brakes
questions.text: The CDL manual identifies one specific type of foundation brake as the most common on heavy commercial vehicles. Which type does the manual call the most common?

answers.text: Wedge brake at every wheel
Air-operated disc brake at every wheel
S-cam drum brake at each wheel
Hydraulic-over-air brake at each wheel

explanations.a: The manual lists wedge brakes as less common than s-cam brakes.
explanations.b: The manual notes air-operated disc brakes are less common than s-cam brakes on heavy CMVs.
explanations.c: The CDL manual states foundation brakes are used at each wheel and that the most common type is the s-cam drum brake.
explanations.d: Hydraulic-over-air conversions are not the manual's stated most-common foundation brake.

questions.name: Air Brakes
questions.text: Some older air brake systems include a small alcohol-injection device. According to the CDL manual, what does the alcohol evaporator do, and how is it serviced?

answers.text: It injects alcohol into engine oil to clean the air compressor; service is annual
It mixes alcohol with the brake lining material and never needs service
It vaporizes alcohol into the cab to keep the driver alert; service is monthly
It puts alcohol into the air system to reduce the risk of ice in valves and other parts in cold weather, with the container checked and filled daily during cold weather

explanations.a: The alcohol evaporator does not service the engine oil; it injects alcohol into the air system.
explanations.b: Alcohol is not added to brake linings; it is added to the air system.
explanations.c: Cab alertness is not the function of the alcohol evaporator.
explanations.d: The CDL manual states some air brake systems have an alcohol evaporator that puts alcohol into the air system to reduce the risk of ice in valves and other parts during cold weather, with the container checked and filled daily during cold weather.

questions.name: Air Brakes
questions.text: Air brake vehicles often have two distinct pressure gauges. According to the CDL manual, what does the supply pressure gauge tell the driver, in contrast to the application pressure gauge?

answers.text: The supply pressure gauge shows how much pressure is in the air tanks; the application pressure gauge shows how much pressure is being applied to the brakes
The supply pressure gauge shows oil pressure to the slack adjuster; the application gauge shows fuel rail pressure
Both gauges read the same pressure but in different units
The supply pressure gauge is for trailer brakes only; the application gauge is for tractor brakes only

explanations.a: The CDL manual states the supply pressure gauge tells you how much air pressure is in the air tanks, while the application pressure gauge shows how much air pressure is being applied to the brakes.
explanations.b: Neither gauge measures oil or fuel pressure.
explanations.c: They read different values: tank pressure versus application pressure.
explanations.d: The gauges are not split tractor-versus-trailer; that distinction is handled by separate dual-system gauges.

questions.name: Air Brakes
questions.text: A visible low air pressure warning signal is required on every CMV with air brakes. According to the CDL manual, the warning must come on before air pressure in the tanks falls below what value?

answers.text: Below 30 psi
Below 60 psi (or one half the compressor governor cutout pressure on older vehicles)
Below 100 psi
Below 125 psi

explanations.a: 30 psi is well below the warning threshold and is in the spring-brake activation range.
explanations.b: The CDL manual states the warning signal must come on before the air pressure in the tanks falls below 60 psi, or below one half the governor cutout pressure on older vehicles.
explanations.c: 100 psi is the typical governor cut-in pressure, not the warning threshold.
explanations.d: 125 psi is the typical governor cut-out pressure, not the warning threshold.

questions.name: Air Brakes
questions.text: Most heavy-duty CMVs are equipped with a dual air brake system for safety. According to the CDL manual, what defines a dual air brake system?

answers.text: Two separate brake pedals that the driver chooses between
One air system shared between the tractor and the trailer
Two separate air brake systems that share a single set of brake controls; each system has its own air tanks, hoses, and lines
A primary air system with a hydraulic backup system

explanations.a: A dual system uses one set of controls, not two separate brake pedals.
explanations.b: Dual refers to two systems on the same vehicle, not the tractor-trailer split.
explanations.c: The CDL manual defines a dual air brake system as two separate air brake systems that use a single set of brake controls; each system has its own air tanks, hoses, and lines.
explanations.d: Dual air systems do not include hydraulic backup; both circuits are pneumatic.

questions.name: Air Brakes
questions.text: While operating a CMV with a dual air brake system on a highway, the driver notices that one of the two air system gauges has dropped well below 60 psi while the other is still normal. According to the CDL manual, what is the correct response?

answers.text: Continue at normal speed because the second system will compensate fully
Apply the parking brake at highway speed to depressurize both systems
Increase speed to reach the next exit before the spring brakes activate
Stop right away and safely park the vehicle, because either the front or rear brakes will not be operating fully and stopping distance will be longer; have the system fixed

explanations.a: The remaining system does not compensate fully; one set of brakes will be inoperative.
explanations.b: Yanking the parking brake at highway speed locks the spring brakes and risks loss of control.
explanations.c: Increasing speed worsens the situation and risks the spring brakes activating in motion.
explanations.d: The CDL manual states that if one air system drops below 60 psi while driving, the driver should stop right away and safely park the vehicle, because either the front or rear brakes will not be operating fully and stopping distance will be longer.

questions.name: Air Brakes
questions.text: Heavy-duty CMVs use dual air brake systems instead of a single circuit for one principal reason. According to the CDL manual, what is that reason?

answers.text: Safety: if one system fails, the driver still has limited braking from the other system
Fuel economy: dual systems use less compressed air per stop
Cargo capacity: dual systems allow heavier loads on the rear axle
Compliance: dual systems are required only for vehicles transporting passengers

explanations.a: The CDL manual states most heavy-duty vehicles use dual air brake systems for safety, so that a failure in one system still leaves limited braking through the other system.
explanations.b: Fuel economy is not the reason given for dual systems.
explanations.c: Cargo capacity is unrelated to brake-system topology.
explanations.d: Dual systems are used on most heavy-duty CMVs, not only passenger vehicles.

questions.name: Air Brakes
questions.text: A typical dual air brake system on a heavy truck divides the two circuits between specific axles. According to the CDL manual, how is the split typically made?

answers.text: One circuit operates the brakes on the steering axle of the trailer; the other operates the trailer parking brakes
One system typically operates the regular brakes on the rear axle or axles, and the other operates the regular brakes on the front axle
One circuit operates only emergency brakes; the other operates only service brakes
One circuit operates only the inside dual tires; the other operates only the outside dual tires

explanations.a: The trailer steering axle is not the typical dual-system divide point in the manual.
explanations.b: The CDL manual states that in a typical dual system, one system operates the regular brakes on the rear axle or axles, and the other operates the regular brakes on the front axle.
explanations.c: Both circuits operate service brakes, not service-versus-emergency.
explanations.d: Inside-versus-outside dual tire splits are not the manual's described dual-system arrangement.

questions.name: Air Brakes
questions.text: On a vehicle equipped with a dual air brake system, the driver monitors air pressure on the dashboard. According to the CDL manual, how are pressure gauges typically arranged?

answers.text: A single gauge with a single needle that reads the lower of the two systems
No gauges at all, only a warning light
A gauge for each half of the system, or a single gauge with two needles
Three gauges: one for each system and one for combined output

explanations.a: A single-needle gauge reading only the lower side does not match the manual's description.
explanations.b: Pressure gauges are required on air brake vehicles, including dual systems.
explanations.c: The CDL manual states a dual system will have a gauge for each half of the system, or a single gauge with two needles.
explanations.d: There is no third combined-output gauge in the standard dual system.

questions.name: Air Brakes
questions.text: After starting the engine on a CMV with a dual air brake system and watching pressure rise on both gauges, the warning light and buzzer should turn off at a specific pressure. According to the CDL manual, what is that turn-off threshold?

answers.text: At any pressure above 30 psi in either system
At any pressure above 100 psi in just one system
At a manufacturer-set value, but only after both systems exceed 150 psi
At a manufacturer-set value that must be greater than 60 psi, when air pressure rises in both systems

explanations.a: 30 psi is below the warning threshold; turning off at that point would leave drivers in danger.
explanations.b: Pressure must be present in both systems, not just one.
explanations.c: The threshold is not 150 psi for either system; it is a manufacturer-set value above 60 psi.
explanations.d: The CDL manual states the warning light and buzzer should shut off when air pressure in both systems rises to a value set by the manufacturer that must be greater than 60 psi.

questions.name: Air Brakes
questions.text: In a dual air brake system, certain components are duplicated between the two circuits. According to the CDL manual, which components does each system have its own copy of?

answers.text: Air tanks, hoses, and lines
Brake pedal and steering wheel
Engine and transmission
Driver instrument cluster and headlights

explanations.a: The CDL manual states each system in a dual setup has its own air tanks, hoses, and lines, while sharing a single set of brake controls.
explanations.b: The brake pedal is shared; the steering wheel is unrelated to the air brake topology.
explanations.c: Powertrain components are not duplicated by the dual system topology.
explanations.d: Instrument clusters and headlights are not duplicated by the brake topology.

questions.name: Air Brakes
questions.text: A driver presses the brake pedal in a CMV with a dual air brake system. The CDL manual describes a specific control arrangement for this kind of system. Which statement matches the manual?

answers.text: The driver must press separate left and right brake pedals to operate each system
The two systems share a single set of brake controls
The driver must select which system to operate via a dashboard switch
The two systems can only be operated by the parking brake control

explanations.a: There are no left and right pedals for the two circuits in a dual system.
explanations.b: The CDL manual states the two systems use a single set of brake controls.
explanations.c: There is no dashboard switch to select between systems.
explanations.d: The parking brake control operates spring brakes, not the dual service brake circuits.

questions.name: Air Brakes
questions.text: The CDL manual instructs CMV drivers to use a specific inspection method when inspecting an air brake vehicle. Which method does the manual describe?

answers.text: A four-step method focused only on the trailer system
A nine-step method that requires towing the vehicle to the inspection station
The basic seven-step inspection procedure described in the manual, with additional air brake items added in their proper steps
A computer-only diagnostic with no manual inspection required

explanations.a: The manual's method is broader than just the trailer system.
explanations.b: The manual does not describe a nine-step method or a tow-in requirement.
explanations.c: The CDL manual instructs drivers to use the basic seven-step inspection procedure, with extra air-brake items added in the order they fit into the seven-step method.
explanations.d: The pre-trip is a hands-on driver inspection, not a computer-only check.

questions.name: Air Brakes
questions.text: During the walk-around portion of an air brake pre-trip, the driver tests the manual slack adjusters by hand. According to the CDL manual, the slack adjuster probably needs adjustment if it moves more than approximately how much where the push rod attaches to it?

answers.text: More than about a quarter of an inch
More than about three inches
Any visible movement at all
More than about one inch where the push rod attaches

explanations.a: A quarter inch is well below the manual's stated threshold.
explanations.b: Three inches is far past the manual's threshold and indicates severe maladjustment.
explanations.c: Some movement is normal; the manual's threshold is one inch where the push rod attaches.
explanations.d: The CDL manual states that if a slack adjuster moves more than about one inch where the push rod attaches to it, it probably needs adjustment.

questions.name: Air Brakes
questions.text: All commercial vehicles built since a specific year are required to have automatic slack adjusters. According to the CDL manual, what is that model-year cutoff?

answers.text: All vehicles built since 1994 have automatic slack adjusters
All vehicles built since 1975 have automatic slack adjusters
All vehicles built since 2005 have automatic slack adjusters
Automatic slack adjusters have never been federally required

explanations.a: The CDL manual states that all vehicles built since 1994 have automatic slack adjusters.
explanations.b: 1975 is associated with the front-brake-limiting-valve era, not automatic slack adjusters.
explanations.c: The 2005 cutoff is not in the manual.
explanations.d: Automatic slack adjusters are required on vehicles built since 1994.

questions.name: Air Brakes
questions.text: During the walk-around portion of an air brake inspection, the driver checks brake drums for cracking. According to the CDL manual, brake drums must not have cracks longer than approximately what fraction of the friction-area width?

answers.text: Cracks longer than one-quarter the width of the friction area
Cracks longer than one-half the width of the friction area
Cracks longer than three-quarters the width of the friction area
Any visible crack of any length is a defect requiring out-of-service

explanations.a: One-quarter is shorter than the manual's stated limit.
explanations.b: The CDL manual states brake drums (or discs) must not have cracks longer than one-half the width of the friction area.
explanations.c: Three-quarters is past the manual's threshold and would represent a severe defect.
explanations.d: Hairline cracks shorter than one-half the friction width are not the manual's defect line.

questions.name: Air Brakes
questions.text: During an air brake walk-around, the driver inspects the brake linings (friction material) for several specific defects. According to the CDL manual, which set of conditions describes a defective lining?

answers.text: Linings that show any color change from heat, regardless of integrity
Linings that show any wear at all on the friction surface
Linings that are loose, soaked with oil or grease, or dangerously thin
Linings whose mounting bolts are fewer than ten in number

explanations.a: Heat discoloration alone is not a defect criterion in the manual.
explanations.b: Some wear is normal; the manual's defect criteria are about loose, contaminated, or dangerously thin material.
explanations.c: The CDL manual states linings must not be loose, must not be soaked with oil or grease, and must not be dangerously thin.
explanations.d: There is no specific bolt-count criterion in the lining inspection.

questions.name: Air Brakes
questions.text: During Step 2 (engine compartment) of the seven-step inspection on a belt-driven air compressor, the CDL manual specifies a particular item to check. Which item is it?

answers.text: The trailer hand valve plumbing
The fifth-wheel kingpin lock
The trailer brake lights
The condition and tightness of the air compressor drive belt, which should be in good condition

explanations.a: Trailer hand-valve plumbing is checked elsewhere, not as part of the compressor drive belt check.
explanations.b: Fifth-wheel components are inspected during the combination-vehicle walk-around, not at the compressor.
explanations.c: Trailer lights are inspected separately from the engine-compartment compressor check.
explanations.d: The CDL manual states that during Step 2 the driver must check the condition and tightness of the air compressor drive belt if the compressor is belt-driven.

questions.name: Air Brakes
questions.text: To test that the low air pressure warning signal works on a CMV with air brakes, the driver follows a specific procedure during the final brake check. Which procedure matches the CDL manual?

answers.text: With the engine off and enough air pressure that the warning is not on, turn the electrical power on, then step on and off the brake pedal to reduce tank pressure; the warning must come on before pressure drops below 60 psi
Idle the engine in neutral and unscrew the safety valve until air bleeds off
Disconnect the trailer service line and watch for the warning to illuminate
Apply and hold the parking brake for at least five minutes

explanations.a: The CDL manual instructs drivers to shut the engine off when pressure is high enough that the warning is not on, turn the electrical power on, and step on and off the brake pedal to reduce tank pressure; the warning must come on before pressure drops below 60 psi.
explanations.b: Unscrewing the safety valve is dangerous and is not the test procedure.
explanations.c: Disconnecting the service line is part of trailer-emergency-brake testing, not the low-pressure-warning test.
explanations.d: Holding the parking brake does not exercise the low-pressure-warning circuit.

questions.name: Air Brakes
questions.text: During the final air brake check, the CDL manual prescribes a slow-moving service-brake test. At about what speed should the driver perform this service-brake test?

answers.text: At highway speed of about 55 mph
Move forward slowly at about 5 mph and apply the brakes firmly
At a stationary 0 mph with the wheels chocked
At about 25 mph in heavy traffic to simulate real conditions

explanations.a: 55 mph is dangerous for a brake-condition test and is not the manual's procedure.
explanations.b: The CDL manual instructs drivers to wait for normal air pressure, release the parking brake, move the vehicle forward slowly at about 5 mph, and apply the brakes firmly using the brake pedal.
explanations.c: A stationary test does not reveal pulling or delayed stopping action.
explanations.d: Real traffic introduces uncontrolled hazards; the manual's test is a controlled low-speed application.

questions.name: Air Brakes
questions.text: To test that the parking brake will hold the vehicle, the CDL manual gives a specific procedure. Which procedure matches the manual?

answers.text: Apply the parking brake at highway speed and observe the deceleration rate
Apply the parking brake on a steep grade with the engine off and the vehicle in neutral
Stop the vehicle, apply the parking brake, and gently pull against it in a low gear to test that the parking brake will hold
Apply the parking brake while spraying water on the brake drums

explanations.a: Yanking the parking brake at highway speed is dangerous and not the test procedure.
explanations.b: The manual's procedure does not require a steep grade or neutral.
explanations.c: The CDL manual instructs drivers to stop the vehicle, put the parking brake on, and gently pull against it in a low gear to test that the parking brake will hold.
explanations.d: Wetting the drums during a parking-brake test is not in the manual.

questions.name: Air Brakes
questions.text: Before checking slack adjusters by hand on a vehicle parked on level ground, the CDL manual specifies a key safety step. Which step is it?

answers.text: Drain all air tanks completely before testing the adjusters
Disconnect the battery to prevent ABS interference
Run the engine at high idle to keep air pressure rising during the test
Park on level ground, chock the wheels to prevent the vehicle from moving, and release the parking brakes so the slack adjusters can be moved

explanations.a: Draining air tanks is unrelated to checking slack adjuster motion.
explanations.b: Disconnecting the battery is not part of the manual's procedure.
explanations.c: Running the engine at high idle does not allow safe slack-adjuster movement.
explanations.d: The CDL manual instructs drivers to park on level ground, chock the wheels, and release the parking brakes so the slack adjusters can be moved by hand.

questions.name: Air Brakes
questions.text: The CDL manual specifies a maximum allowable static air leakage rate for a single vehicle with air brakes. With a fully charged system, engine off, and parking brake released, what is the maximum allowable leakage in one minute?

answers.text: Less than 2 psi in one minute for a single vehicle
Less than 5 psi in one minute for a single vehicle
Less than 10 psi in one minute for a single vehicle
Any leakage rate is acceptable as long as the warning light does not come on

explanations.a: The CDL manual states the static leakage rate for a single vehicle should be less than 2 psi in one minute.
explanations.b: 5 psi in one minute is too much for a single vehicle and exceeds the manual's limit.
explanations.c: 10 psi in one minute is well above the static leakage threshold.
explanations.d: There is a specific psi-per-minute leakage limit, regardless of warning-light state.

questions.name: Air Brakes
questions.text: For a combination vehicle, the CDL manual sets a different static air leakage limit than for a single vehicle. With a fully charged system and engine off, what is the maximum allowable static leakage rate for a combination vehicle?

answers.text: Less than 1 psi in one minute
Less than 3 psi in one minute
Less than 6 psi in one minute
Less than 12 psi in one minute

explanations.a: 1 psi in one minute is stricter than the combination-vehicle standard; that figure is below the manual's limit.
explanations.b: The CDL manual states the static leakage rate for a combination vehicle should be less than 3 psi in one minute.
explanations.c: 6 psi in one minute exceeds the combination-vehicle limit by double.
explanations.d: 12 psi in one minute is far above the manual's limit.

questions.name: Air Brakes
questions.text: With the foot brake fully applied for one minute on a CMV, the CDL manual gives a separate set of leakage limits for both single and combination vehicles. Which pair matches the manual's applied-leakage standard?

answers.text: More than 5 psi for a single vehicle and more than 7 psi for a combination vehicle
More than 1 psi for a single vehicle and more than 2 psi for a combination vehicle
More than 3 psi in one minute is too much for a single vehicle, and more than 4 psi in one minute is too much for a combination vehicle
More than 8 psi for a single vehicle and more than 10 psi for a combination vehicle

explanations.a: 5 psi and 7 psi are well above the manual's applied-leakage limits.
explanations.b: 1 psi and 2 psi are below the manual's applied-leakage limits, which are 3 and 4 psi respectively.
explanations.c: The CDL manual states with the foot brake fully applied that an air pressure drop of more than 3 psi in one minute is too much for a single vehicle, and more than 4 psi in one minute is too much for a combination vehicle.
explanations.d: 8 psi and 10 psi are far above the manual's applied-leakage limits.

questions.name: Air Brakes
questions.text: To perform the static air leakage test correctly, the CDL manual sets out a specific sequence. Which procedure matches the manual?

answers.text: Drain all tanks first, then build pressure to 60 psi, leave the engine running, and time the leakage rate
Apply the parking brake, leave engine running at full throttle, and time the leakage rate at the trailer hand valve
Disconnect the trailer, apply hand valve, and time leakage at the air dryer drain
With a fully charged air system (typically 125 psi), turn off the engine, release the parking brake, and time the air pressure drop

explanations.a: Building only to 60 psi misses the full-charge starting point and leaving the engine running invalidates the static test.
explanations.b: Running at full throttle continues to charge the system and invalidates the static leakage measurement.
explanations.c: Disconnecting the trailer changes the volume of the system and is not the manual's procedure.
explanations.d: The CDL manual instructs drivers to perform the static leakage test with a fully charged air system (typically 125 psi), engine off, parking brake released, and time the air pressure drop.

questions.name: Air Brakes
questions.text: During the air brake check, the CDL manual gives a target buildup time for dual air systems with the engine at operating rpms. Which target matches the manual?

answers.text: Pressure should build from 85 to 100 psi within 45 seconds in dual air systems
Pressure should build from 0 to 60 psi within 5 seconds
Pressure should build from 50 to 90 psi within 10 seconds
Pressure should build from 60 to 125 psi within 5 minutes

explanations.a: The CDL manual states that with the engine at operating rpms, pressure should build from 85 to 100 psi within 45 seconds in dual air systems.
explanations.b: 5 seconds for that pressure swing is far too fast and not in the manual.
explanations.c: 50-to-90-psi-in-10-seconds is not the manual's standard for dual systems.
explanations.d: 5 minutes is far too slow and would indicate a major defect.

questions.name: Air Brakes
questions.text: For pre-1975 single-air-system vehicles, the CDL manual gives a different pressure buildup standard with the engine at idle. Which standard matches the manual?

answers.text: Pressure should build from 85 to 100 psi within 30 seconds
Pressure should build from 50 to 90 psi within 3 minutes with engine idle of 600 to 900 rpm
Pressure should build from 0 to 125 psi within 15 seconds
There is no published standard for pre-1975 single air systems

explanations.a: The 85-to-100 standard applies to dual air systems, not pre-1975 single systems.
explanations.b: The CDL manual states for pre-1975 single air systems, typical requirements are pressure buildup from 50 to 90 psi within 3 minutes with the engine at an idle speed of 600 to 900 rpm.
explanations.c: 15 seconds is far too aggressive for the pre-1975 single-system standard.
explanations.d: The manual does publish a pre-1975 standard.

questions.name: Air Brakes
questions.text: During the air brake check, the CDL manual instructs drivers to verify the air compressor governor cut-out pressure. According to the manual, the compressor should typically stop pumping at approximately what pressure?

answers.text: At about 60 psi
At about 100 psi
At about 125 psi (verify against the manufacturer's specifications)
At about 200 psi

explanations.a: 60 psi is the low-pressure-warning threshold, not the governor cut-out point.
explanations.b: 100 psi is the typical governor cut-in pressure.
explanations.c: The CDL manual states pumping by the air compressor should stop at about 125 psi at cut-out, with verification against the manufacturer's specifications.
explanations.d: 200 psi exceeds typical air brake operating range and the safety valve would relieve well before that.

questions.name: Air Brakes
questions.text: After completing the air leakage rate test, a driver discovers the rate exceeds the published limit. According to the CDL manual, what is the proper response before driving?

answers.text: Drive at reduced speed to the next service stop, then have the leak fixed
Drive normally because the leakage will likely seal itself with use
Apply the parking brake while driving to compensate for the leak
Check for air leaks and have them fixed before driving the vehicle, otherwise the brakes could be lost while driving

explanations.a: Driving at reduced speed with excessive leakage is not the manual's instruction.
explanations.b: Air leaks do not self-seal; the manual specifically warns drivers not to drive until the leak is fixed.
explanations.c: Driving with the parking brake applied can damage the spring brakes and is not a leak compensation technique.
explanations.d: The CDL manual states drivers must check for air leaks and have them fixed before driving the vehicle, otherwise the driver could lose the brakes while driving.

questions.name: Air Brakes
questions.text: Spring brakes are designed to apply automatically when air pressure falls below a certain range. According to the CDL manual, at what pressure range do tractor and straight truck spring brakes typically come fully on?

answers.text: In the range of 20 to 45 psi (typically 20 to 30 psi for tractor and straight truck)
In the range of 60 to 80 psi
In the range of 100 to 125 psi
Spring brakes do not activate based on pressure

explanations.a: The CDL manual states tractor and straight truck spring brakes will come fully on when air pressure drops to a range of 20 to 45 psi (typically 20 to 30 psi).
explanations.b: 60 to 80 psi is well above the spring-brake activation range.
explanations.c: 100 to 125 psi is the typical operating pressure range, not the spring-brake activation range.
explanations.d: Spring brakes are specifically pressure-actuated for emergency use.

questions.name: Air Brakes
questions.text: The CDL manual gives a specific warning about combining the brake pedal with spring brakes that are already applied. Which warning matches the manual?

answers.text: Push the brake pedal hard while spring brakes are on to test the system
Never push the brake pedal down when the spring brakes are on, because the brakes could be damaged by the combined forces of the springs and air pressure
Always push the brake pedal halfway when spring brakes are on for parking
Push the brake pedal three times before releasing spring brakes

explanations.a: The manual specifically warns against pushing the brake pedal while spring brakes are applied.
explanations.b: The CDL manual cautions never to push the brake pedal down when the spring brakes are on, because the brakes could be damaged by the combined forces of the springs and air pressure.
explanations.c: Halfway pedal pressure with spring brakes engaged still risks the same damage.
explanations.d: There is no three-pump procedure in the manual.

questions.name: Air Brakes
questions.text: The CDL manual describes a specific dashboard control on newer vehicles for applying and releasing the parking brakes. Which description matches the manual?

answers.text: A green push-button labeled 'park'
A red rocker switch on the console
A diamond-shaped, yellow, push-pull control knob; pull out to apply, push in to release
A foot-actuated lever to the left of the brake pedal

explanations.a: The CDL manual specifies a yellow diamond push-pull control, not a green push-button.
explanations.b: A red rocker switch is not the parking-brake control described in the manual.
explanations.c: The CDL manual states that on newer vehicles with air brakes, drivers put on the parking brakes using a diamond-shaped, yellow, push-pull control knob, pulling it out to apply and pushing it in to release.
explanations.d: The parking brake is hand-operated on the dash, not a foot-actuated lever.

questions.name: Air Brakes
questions.text: All trucks, truck tractors, and buses must be equipped with emergency and parking brakes. According to the CDL manual, what specific holding mechanism is required because air pressure can eventually leak away?

answers.text: They must be held by a vacuum reservoir for at least one hour
They must be held by an electromagnet powered by the battery
They must be held by an electronic latch with a backup capacitor
They must be held on by mechanical force, because air pressure can eventually leak away

explanations.a: There is no vacuum-reservoir holding mechanism specified in the manual.
explanations.b: Electromagnetic holding is not the manual's mechanism for emergency and parking brakes.
explanations.c: Electronic latches are not the manual's required holding mechanism.
explanations.d: The CDL manual states emergency brakes and parking brakes must be held on by mechanical force, because air pressure can eventually leak away; spring brakes are usually used to meet these needs.

questions.name: Air Brakes
questions.text: The CDL manual describes how the emergency brake system functions in relation to the service and parking brake systems. Which description matches the manual?

answers.text: The emergency brake system uses parts of the service and parking brake systems to stop the vehicle in a brake system failure
The emergency brake is an entirely separate hydraulic circuit
The emergency brake operates only the trailer brakes via a separate compressor
The emergency brake is engaged solely by an electronic ABS module

explanations.a: The CDL manual states the emergency brake system uses parts of the service and parking brake systems to stop the vehicle in a brake system failure.
explanations.b: The emergency brake is not a separate hydraulic circuit on a standard air-braked CMV.
explanations.c: The emergency brake is not limited to trailer-only operation through a separate compressor.
explanations.d: ABS is anti-lock control, not the emergency brake mechanism.

questions.name: Air Brakes
questions.text: The CDL manual identifies two specific situations in which a driver should not use the parking brake. Which situations does the manual warn about?

answers.text: When parked on level paved ground or in a public garage
When the brakes are very hot from just having come down a steep grade, or when the brakes are very wet in freezing temperatures
When the engine is running, or when the parking lights are on
When the trailer is empty, or when the cargo doors are open

explanations.a: Level paved ground is a normal place to use the parking brake.
explanations.b: The CDL manual warns drivers not to use the parking brakes if the brakes are very hot from coming down a steep grade, or if the brakes are very wet in freezing temperatures.
explanations.c: Engine state or parking-light state is unrelated to parking-brake use.
explanations.d: Trailer load and door state are unrelated to whether the parking brake should be used.

questions.name: Air Brakes
questions.text: Some CMVs include a special control that lets the driver apply the spring brakes gradually rather than all at once. According to the CDL manual, what is this control called and how does it operate?

answers.text: It is called a tractor protection valve and slams the spring brakes on at maximum force only
It is called the trailer hand valve and operates the trailer service brakes only
It is called a modulating control valve, is spring-loaded for feel, and applies the spring brakes harder as the lever is moved further
It is called the glad hand and connects only to the trailer emergency line

explanations.a: The tractor protection valve has a different function and does not gradually apply spring brakes.
explanations.b: The trailer hand valve operates only the trailer service brakes, not spring brakes.
explanations.c: The CDL manual describes the modulating control valve as spring-loaded for feel, with the spring brakes coming on harder the more the control lever is moved.
explanations.d: Glad hands are pneumatic couplers between tractor and trailer, not spring-brake controls.

questions.name: Air Brakes
questions.text: While driving down the road, the low air pressure warning illuminates on a CMV. According to the CDL manual, what should the driver do, and why?

answers.text: Continue driving until the gauge reaches 30 psi to confirm the warning is real
Turn off the warning lamp and continue to the destination
Increase engine rpm and apply the brakes repeatedly to rebuild pressure
Stop and safely park the vehicle as soon as possible, since controlled braking is possible only while enough air remains in the tanks and the spring brakes will activate at 20 to 45 psi

explanations.a: Waiting until 30 psi means the spring brakes may activate suddenly, possibly causing a skid in a heavily loaded or lightly loaded vehicle.
explanations.b: Turning off the warning does not address the underlying air loss.
explanations.c: Brake applications consume more air than they save and worsen the situation.
explanations.d: The CDL manual states that if the low air pressure warning comes on, the driver should stop and safely park the vehicle as soon as possible because controlled braking is possible only while enough air remains, and spring brakes will activate at 20 to 45 psi.

questions.name: Air Brakes
questions.text: For a routine stop in a CMV with air brakes, the CDL manual describes a specific normal-stop technique. Which technique matches the manual?

answers.text: Push the brake pedal down and control the pressure so the vehicle comes to a smooth, safe stop; if manual transmission, do not push the clutch in until engine rpm is down close to idle
Apply maximum pedal pressure all the way to the stop, then push the clutch in
Pump the brake pedal rapidly through the entire stop
Coast in neutral until the vehicle stops itself

explanations.a: The CDL manual describes the normal stop as pushing the pedal down, controlling pressure for a smooth stop, and on manual transmissions, not pushing the clutch in until engine rpm is close to idle.
explanations.b: Maximum pedal pressure on a routine stop is harsh, can lock the wheels, and is not the normal-stop technique.
explanations.c: Pumping the pedal through a normal stop wastes air and is not the manual's technique.
explanations.d: Coasting in neutral removes engine braking and is not the manual's normal-stop technique.

questions.name: Air Brakes
questions.text: In an emergency stop, the CDL manual describes a primary objective for how the vehicle should behave under braking. Which objective matches the manual?

answers.text: The vehicle should jackknife to spread cargo across the largest possible area
Brake in a way that keeps the vehicle in a straight line and allows the driver to turn if it becomes necessary
The vehicle should slide sideways to slow more quickly through aerodynamic drag
The vehicle should pivot on its drive wheels to face oncoming traffic

explanations.a: Jackknifing is a loss-of-control failure, not the emergency-braking objective.
explanations.b: The CDL manual instructs drivers to brake in a way that keeps the vehicle in a straight line and allows the driver to turn if necessary.
explanations.c: Sliding sideways is a skid; the manual's objective is straight-line stopping.
explanations.d: Pivoting toward oncoming traffic is unsafe and not the manual's objective.

questions.name: Air Brakes
questions.text: One of the two emergency-stop methods the CDL manual recommends is called controlled braking. Which description matches the manual's controlled-braking method?

answers.text: Apply the parking brake gradually until the vehicle stops
Pump the brakes ten times in rapid succession regardless of wheel state
Apply the brakes as hard as you can without locking the wheels, keep steering wheel movements very small, and release the brakes if you must make a larger steering adjustment or if the wheels lock
Hold the brake pedal at exactly half travel for the entire emergency stop

explanations.a: Controlled braking does not use the parking brake; it uses the service-brake pedal.
explanations.b: Pumping ten times regardless of wheel state is not the manual's technique.
explanations.c: The CDL manual describes controlled braking as applying the brakes as hard as you can without locking the wheels, keeping steering wheel movements very small, and releasing the brakes if a larger steering adjustment is needed or the wheels lock.
explanations.d: Half-travel pedal hold is not the manual's controlled-braking technique.

questions.name: Air Brakes
questions.text: The second emergency-stop method described in the CDL manual is stab braking. Which description matches the manual's stab-braking method, including its critical timing detail?

answers.text: Apply the brakes lightly for ten seconds, then release for ten seconds, and repeat
Apply only the trailer hand valve and ignore the foot brake
Apply the parking brake fully, release after one second, and repeat

Apply the brakes all the way; release the brakes when the wheels lock up; as soon as the wheels start rolling, apply the brakes fully again — but it can take up to one second for the wheels to start rolling, so do not re-apply until they have

explanations.a: The manual does not use a fixed 10-on/10-off pattern.
explanations.b: Stab braking uses the foot brake, not just the trailer hand valve.
explanations.c: Stab braking uses the service brakes, not the parking brake.
explanations.d: The CDL manual describes stab braking as applying the brakes all the way, releasing when the wheels lock, then re-applying once the wheels start rolling — noting it can take up to one second for the wheels to start rolling, and re-applying before they do means the vehicle will not straighten out.

questions.name: Air Brakes
questions.text: Air brakes introduce a specific delay that hydraulic brakes do not have. According to the CDL manual, what is brake lag, and approximately how long is it?

answers.text: Brake lag is the time required for the brakes to work after the brake pedal is pushed; with air brakes it takes about half a second or more for the air to flow through the lines
Brake lag is the wear on the lining over the life of the brake; about ten years
Brake lag is the time it takes the parking brake to fully apply when set; about three minutes
Brake lag is the delay between cutting power and reaching idle speed; about ten seconds

explanations.a: The CDL manual defines brake lag as the time required for the brakes to work after the brake pedal is pushed; with air brakes it takes about half a second or more for the air to flow through the lines to the brakes.
explanations.b: Lining wear is not what brake lag refers to in the manual.
explanations.c: Parking brake application time is not the definition of brake lag.
explanations.d: Engine idle delay is not the manual's definition of brake lag.

questions.name: Air Brakes
questions.text: The CDL manual gives a specific distance figure for the brake-lag component at 55 mph on dry pavement. About how many feet does air brake lag add to total stopping distance at 55 mph?

answers.text: About 5 feet
About 32 feet
About 100 feet
About 250 feet

explanations.a: 5 feet underestimates the manual's stated brake-lag distance at 55 mph.
explanations.b: The CDL manual states the air brake lag distance at 55 mph on dry pavement adds about 32 feet to the total stopping distance.
explanations.c: 100 feet overstates the lag-distance figure given in the manual.
explanations.d: 250 feet is roughly the low-beam range from Section 2, not the brake-lag figure.

questions.name: Air Brakes
questions.text: Adding perception, reaction, brake-lag, and braking distances together for an air-braked CMV at 55 mph, the CDL manual gives a specific total. What is that total?

answers.text: About 250 feet, the low-beam sight range
About 350 feet, less than a football field
Over 450 feet for an average driver under good traction and brake conditions
About 200 feet at 55 mph

explanations.a: 250 feet is the low-beam range, not the air-brake total stopping distance.
explanations.b: 350 feet is less than the manual's combined total at 55 mph.
explanations.c: The CDL manual states that at 55 mph for an average driver under good traction and brake conditions, the total stopping distance for an air-braked CMV is over 450 feet, after adding perception, reaction, brake lag, and braking distances.
explanations.d: 200 feet is much less than the actual total at 55 mph.

questions.name: Air Brakes
questions.text: On a long downgrade, brakes can fade due to excessive heat. According to the CDL manual, what specific physical changes occur during brake fade?

answers.text: The brake chamber rusts and seizes within minutes of overheating
The slack adjuster snaps under thermal stress within seconds
The wiring to the ABS module melts and disconnects all braking
Heat causes chemical changes in the brake lining that reduce friction, and overheated brake drums expand so the shoes have to move farther to contact the drums, with reduced contact force

explanations.a: Brake chambers do not rust and seize from a single hot descent in the manner described.
explanations.b: Slack adjusters do not typically snap from heat in the time scale of brake fade.
explanations.c: ABS wiring is not the failure mode the manual describes for brake fade.
explanations.d: The CDL manual states brake fade results from chemical changes in the brake lining that reduce friction, and from expansion of overheated brake drums so that the shoes must move farther to make contact with reduced force.

questions.name: Air Brakes
questions.objective: 4.7 Air brake test for the licensing exam
questions.text: The CDL manual lists a sequence of checks that replace the hydraulic-brake check at Step 7 of the seven-step pre-trip inspection on an air-braked CMV. Which list matches the manual's air-brake final check?

answers.text: Test low pressure warning, check spring brakes come on automatically, check pressure buildup rate, test air leakage rate, check governor cut-in/cut-out, test parking brake, test service brakes
Drain all tanks, fill with alcohol, lubricate slack adjusters, replace brake pads
Disconnect trailer, idle engine, sound horn, check headlights
Apply parking brake only, then drive at 55 mph and apply emergency brake

explanations.a: The CDL manual lists the air-brake final check as testing the low pressure warning, checking spring brakes come on automatically, checking pressure buildup rate, testing air leakage rate, checking governor cut-in/cut-out, testing the parking brake, and testing service brakes.
explanations.b: Draining tanks and refilling with alcohol is not the final-check procedure.
explanations.c: Disconnecting the trailer and sounding the horn are not part of the final check.
explanations.d: Applying the emergency brake at highway speed is dangerous and not in the procedure.

questions.name: Air Brakes
questions.objective: 4.7 Air brake test for the licensing exam
questions.text: The CDL manual prescribes a specific order for the parking and service brake tests within the air-brake final check. Which order matches the manual?

answers.text: Service brake test first, then parking brake test
Parking brake test first (gentle pull against in low gear), then service brake test (forward at about 5 mph and apply firmly)
The two tests are interchangeable and may be performed in any order
Both tests are performed simultaneously while the vehicle is stationary

explanations.a: The manual lists the parking brake test before the service brake test.
explanations.b: The CDL manual instructs drivers to test the parking brake first by gently pulling against it in low gear, then to test the service brakes by moving forward at about 5 mph and applying them firmly.
explanations.c: The manual presents a specific order; the tests are not interchangeable.
explanations.d: The service brake test requires forward motion, which cannot occur while the vehicle is stationary.

questions.name: Air Brakes
questions.objective: 4.7 Air brake test for the licensing exam
questions.text: To verify the low pressure warning during the licensing exam's air brake test, the CDL manual specifies a particular pedal action with the engine off. Which action matches the manual?

answers.text: Push the pedal once and hold it for one full minute
Hold the pedal at exactly half travel until the warning sounds
Step on and off the brake pedal to reduce air tank pressure until the warning comes on; the warning must come on before pressure drops below 60 psi
Tap the pedal once at 10-second intervals while the parking brake is engaged

explanations.a: A single one-minute hold is not the manual's procedure for fanning down pressure.
explanations.b: Half-travel pedal hold is not the manual's stated test action.
explanations.c: The CDL manual instructs drivers to step on and off the brake pedal to reduce air tank pressure until the warning illuminates; the warning must come on before pressure drops below 60 psi.
explanations.d: Tapping with the parking brake engaged is not the manual's procedure.

questions.name: Air Brakes
questions.objective: 4.7 Air brake test for the licensing exam
questions.text: After verifying the low pressure warning during the air-brake test, the CDL manual instructs the driver to keep reducing pressure to confirm a specific spring-brake event. What event does the driver verify?

answers.text: That the engine restarts automatically when pressure drops below 30 psi
That the trailer brakes release independently of the tractor
That the safety valve opens and discharges air to atmosphere
That the tractor protection valve and parking brake valve close (pop out) at the manufacturer's specification (20 to 45 psi), causing the spring brakes to come on

explanations.a: There is no automatic engine restart at any pressure level in this test.
explanations.b: Trailer brake release independent of the tractor is not what is being verified here.
explanations.c: Safety valve actuation is not the spring-brake test event.
explanations.d: The CDL manual instructs drivers to continue fanning off air pressure until the tractor protection valve and parking brake valve close (pop out) at the manufacturer's specification of 20 to 45 psi, causing the spring brakes to come on.

questions.name: Air Brakes
questions.objective: 4.7 Air brake test for the licensing exam
questions.keyword: parking brake test in low gear
questions.text: During the parking-brake portion of the air-brake test, the CDL manual instructs the driver to do something specific to confirm the parking brake will hold. Which action matches the manual?

answers.text: Apply the parking brake and gently pull against it in a low gear to confirm it holds the vehicle
Apply the parking brake while idling in neutral with the clutch fully depressed
Apply the parking brake while accelerating to highway speed in fifth gear
Apply the parking brake and rock the vehicle by hand from outside the cab

explanations.a: The CDL manual instructs drivers to apply the parking brake and gently pull against it in a low gear to confirm it holds the vehicle.
explanations.b: Sitting in neutral with the clutch in does not test the parking brake's holding ability.
explanations.c: Pulling against the parking brake at highway speed is dangerous and not the test procedure.
explanations.d: Rocking the vehicle from outside is not the manual's parking-brake test.

questions.name: Air Brakes
questions.objective: 4.7 Air brake test for the licensing exam
questions.text: During the service-brake portion of the air-brake test, the CDL manual instructs the driver to watch for several specific abnormalities. Which set of abnormalities matches the manual?

answers.text: Check for unusual smells from the cab and any vibration in the steering wheel
Note any vehicle pulling to one side, unusual feel, or delayed stopping action
Note tire-pressure changes and suspension noise during the stop
Note any change in instrument-panel lights or radio reception

explanations.a: Cab smells and steering vibration are not the listed signs in the manual's service-brake test.
explanations.b: The CDL manual instructs drivers to note any vehicle pulling to one side, unusual feel, or delayed stopping action during the service-brake test.
explanations.c: Tire pressure and suspension noise are not the manual's specified service-brake-test indicators.
explanations.d: Instrument-panel lights and radio reception are unrelated to the service-brake test.

questions.name: Air Brakes
questions.objective: 4.7 Air brake test for the licensing exam
questions.text: The CDL manual explains the value of the in-motion service-brake test as part of the air-brake check. According to the manual, what does this test reveal?

answers.text: It reveals the exact stopping distance to the inch
It reveals tire-tread depth to the nearest 1/32 of an inch
It may show problems the driver otherwise would not know about until the brakes were needed on the road
It reveals fuel consumption per mile under braking

explanations.a: The test does not measure stopping distance to the inch; it is a qualitative observation.
explanations.b: Tread depth is measured during a separate tire inspection, not by the service-brake test.
explanations.c: The CDL manual states the in-motion service-brake test may show problems the driver otherwise would not know about until needing the brakes on the road.
explanations.d: Fuel consumption is not what this test measures.

questions.name: Air Brakes
questions.objective: 4.7 Air brake test for the licensing exam
questions.text: To pass the air-brake licensing exam, the driver must demonstrate the full final-check sequence in order. Which sequence below most closely matches the CDL manual's order?

answers.text: Service brake test, parking brake test, governor check, leakage rate, spring brakes, low pressure warning, pressure buildup
Drain tanks, refill alcohol, replace pads, refit drums, retorque slack adjusters
Idle test only, with no in-motion verification of any kind

Test low pressure warning, check spring brakes come on automatically, check rate of air pressure buildup, test air leakage rate, check governor cut-in and cut-out, test parking brake, test service brakes

explanations.a: The order in this option places the service and parking brake tests at the front, contrary to the manual.
explanations.b: That option lists maintenance tasks, not the air-brake final check sequence.
explanations.c: The manual requires in-motion verification of service brakes; idle-only testing is incomplete.
explanations.d: The CDL manual's order for the air-brake final check is: test low pressure warning, check that spring brakes come on automatically, check rate of air pressure buildup, test air leakage rate, check governor cut-in and cut-out, test parking brake, then test service brakes.
